explain: A plural subject in the nominative: _Dī_.
distractors: Deus Rōmam amant.
_Deus_ is singular (“the god”). A plural subject in the nominative: _Dī_.
Deum Rōmam amant.
_Deum_ is accusative singular. A plural subject in the nominative: _Dī_.
Deōs Rōmam amant.
_Deōs_ is accusative plural. A plural subject in the nominative: _Dī_.

explain: The one who has is the subject, nominative: _Dea_.
distractors: Deus magnam potestātem habet.
_Deus_ is masculine (“god”). The one who has is the subject, nominative: _Dea_.
Deam magnam potestātem habet.
_Deam_ is accusative. The one who has is the subject, nominative: _Dea_.
Deae magnam potestātem habet.
_Deae_ is genitive or dative. The one who has is the subject, nominative: _Dea_.

explain: _ōrō_ takes the accusative: the ones prayed to: _Deōs_.
distractors: Dī ōrāmus.
_Dī_ is nominative plural. _ōrō_ takes the accusative: the ones prayed to: _Deōs_.
Deum ōrāmus.
_Deum_ is singular. _ōrō_ takes the accusative: the ones prayed to: _Deōs_.
Deōrum ōrāmus.
_Deōrum_ is genitive plural. _ōrō_ takes the accusative: the ones prayed to: _Deōs_.

en: The altar is in the temple.
distractors: Āra in templum est.
_templum_ is accusative. After _in_ meaning “in”, use the ablative: _templō_.
Āra in templī est.
_templī_ is genitive. After _in_ meaning “in”, use the ablative: _templō_.
Āra in templa est.
_templa_ is plural. After _in_ meaning “in”, use the ablative: _templō_.
Nēmō fātō vincit.
_fātō_ is dative or ablative. The thing conquered is accusative: _fātum_.
Nēmō fātī vincit.
_fātī_ is genitive. The thing conquered is accusative: _fātum_.
Nēmō fātīs vincit.
_fātīs_ is dative or ablative plural. The thing conquered is accusative: _fātum_.

en: The gods are in the sky.
distractors: Dī in caelum sunt.
_caelum_ is accusative. After _in_ meaning “in”, use the ablative: _caelō_.
Dī in caelī sunt.
_caelī_ is genitive. After _in_ meaning “in”, use the ablative: _caelō_.
Dī in caelōrum sunt.
_caelōrum_ is genitive plural. After _in_ meaning “in”, use the ablative: _caelō_.

en: The sun and the moon are in the sky.
la: Sōl et lūna in caelō sunt.
explain: The second subject is also nominative: _lūna_.
distractors: Sōl et lūnam in caelō sunt.
_lūnam_ is accusative. The second subject is also nominative: _lūna_.
Sōl et lūnae in caelō sunt.
_lūnae_ is genitive or dative. The second subject is also nominative: _lūna_.
Sōl et lūnās in caelō sunt.
_lūnās_ is accusative plural. The second subject is also nominative: _lūna_.

en: The citizen gives a gift to the god.
distractors: Cīvis deum mūnus dat.
_deum_ is accusative. The one receiving is dative: _deō_.
Cīvis deus mūnus dat.
_deus_ is nominative. The one receiving is dative: _deō_.
Cīvis deī mūnus dat.
_deī_ is genitive or plural. The one receiving is dative: _deō_.
Deus vōx audit.
_vōx_ is nominative. The thing heard is accusative: _vōcem_.
Deus vōcis audit.
_vōcis_ is genitive. The thing heard is accusative: _vōcem_.
Deus vōcī audit.
_vōcī_ is dative. The thing heard is accusative: _vōcem_.

en: They fear the anger of the gods.
explain: “The anger of the gods” needs the genitive plural: _deōrum_.
distractors: Īram deōs timent.
_deōs_ is accusative plural. “The anger of the gods” needs the genitive plural: _deōrum_.
Īram Dīs timent.
_Dīs_ is dative plural. “The anger of the gods” needs the genitive plural: _deōrum_.
Īram deus timent.
_deus_ is nominative singular. “The anger of the gods” needs the genitive plural: _deōrum_.

en: The gods hold the fate of men.
explain: “The fate of men” needs the genitive plural: _hominum_.
distractors: Dī fāta hominēs tenent.
_hominēs_ is nominative or accusative plural. “The fate of men” needs the genitive plural: _hominum_.
Dī fāta hominibus tenent.
_hominibus_ is dative or ablative plural. “The fate of men” needs the genitive plural: _hominum_.
Dī fāta hominem tenent.
_hominem_ is accusative singular. “The fate of men” needs the genitive plural: _hominum_.

en: The altar of the goddess is great.
explain: “The altar of the goddess” needs the genitive: _deae_.
distractors: Āra dea magna est.
_dea_ is nominative. “The altar of the goddess” needs the genitive: _deae_.
Āra deam magna est.
_deam_ is accusative. “The altar of the goddess” needs the genitive: _deae_.
Āra deābus magna est.
_deābus_ is dative or ablative plural. “The altar of the goddess” needs the genitive: _deae_.
